gaps.symptom: The harness benchmarked full pages but did not originally include a first-class component atlas showing how each style treats buttons, inputs, chips, cards, rails, and interactive states.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry review has focused on full-surface composition more than cross-style component-system comparison.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add a first-class style atlas workflow that compares component behavior, geometry, state language, and density across style families alongside full-page fixtures.

gaps.symptom: The current harness over-indexed on hard-edge, low-radius component geometry and underrepresented rounded systems such as Material-style surfaces.
gaps.likely_root_cause: The style catalog favored editorial, enterprise, and brutalist directions before adding a tactile rounded-system benchmark.
gaps.recommended_fix: Expand canonical style coverage to include rounded, tactile systems and make geometry variation a first-class style-fidelity check.

gaps.symptom: Background texture patterns were reused too freely as a quick way to differentiate surfaces, which made several pages feel templated instead of style-specific.
gaps.likely_root_cause: The runtime and harness do not yet distinguish between a deliberate surface texture and a generic grid-overlay fallback.
gaps.recommended_fix: Teach design-audit to flag repeated texture overlays and require surface texture to be justified by the chosen style family.

gaps.symptom: The harness now depends on a large external style reference intake, but Foundry still lacks a first-class normalized style catalog that the design runtime can query directly.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Style research is being normalized inside the repo harness instead of inside a reusable runtime data layer shared by design workflows.
gaps.recommended_fix: Promote Design Prompts-style normalization into a first-class Foundry dataset pipeline with explicit source metadata, mappings, and anti-pattern fields.

gaps.symptom: The harness can describe style drift, but style fidelity still depends on manually assigned scorecard numbers rather than a runtime scoring dimension.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry QA primitives capture evidence and screenshots, but they do not yet score whether a surface remained faithful to a restrained, editorial, industrial, or other chosen style family.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add style-fidelity checks to design-audit and the UI harness so each scenario can fail when it drifts back to generic product defaults.

gaps.symptom: The UI harness can now emit derived runtime traces, but Foundry's underlying design runtime still does not natively emit first-class provenance for style selection, exclusions, remediation steps, and dataset usage.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Benchmark routing can derive trace artifacts from scenario contracts, but the design engine itself still lacks a runtime-native provenance layer.
gaps.recommended_fix: Promote prompt-trace generation into the core design runtime and attach dataset ids, exclusions, remediation skills, and style reference ids automatically.

gaps.symptom: The UI harness can now derive remediation routing, but Foundry still lacks a native runtime that executes second-pass design remediation automatically after a weak first pass.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry has a command layer for design remediation and harness-level routing, but no shared runtime that can diagnose a surface and execute the right second-pass skills end-to-end.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add a first-class design remediation runtime that chains audit, layout repair, typography repair, intensity adjustment, simplification, and polish with explicit execution traces.

gaps.symptom: Foundry now has a first-class ui-testing route and a single benchmark runner, but the execution path still lives in repo-local harness scripts instead of a shared Foundry runtime or CLI executor.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Workflow routing and runner consolidation exist, but the benchmark runtime is still implemented in repo-local scripts rather than a reusable shared execution layer.
gaps.recommended_fix: Promote the repo-local benchmark runner into a native ui-testing runtime or CLI surface that the shared route can execute directly.

gaps.symptom: Responsive quality is visible in screenshots but not automatically scored by existing Foundry QA primitives.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Web QA captures evidence but lacks a built-in rubric for mobile re-composition quality.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add viewport-aware scoring hooks and responsive heuristics to the harness workflow.

gaps.symptom: The first atelier-stay layout let the hero headline dominate the spread so heavily that the supporting editorial modules looked underweighted until the type scale and column proportions were manually rebalanced.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry can produce technically valid editorial grids without checking whether headline mass and adjacent module density stay in visual parity.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add composition-balance checks to design-audit so oversized editorial headlines and underweighted companion columns fail review before screenshots are approved.

gaps.recommended_fix: Teach design-audit to flag repeated texture overlays and require surface texture to be justified by the chosen style family.

gaps.symptom: The harness now depends on a large external style reference intake, but Foundry still lacks a first-class normalized style catalog that the design runtime can query directly.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Style research is being normalized inside the repo harness instead of inside a reusable runtime data layer shared by design workflows.
gaps.recommended_fix: Promote Design Prompts-style normalization into a first-class Foundry dataset pipeline with explicit source metadata, mappings, and anti-pattern fields.

gaps.symptom: The harness can describe style drift, but style fidelity still depends on manually assigned scorecard numbers rather than a runtime scoring dimension.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry QA primitives capture evidence and screenshots, but they do not yet score whether a surface remained faithful to a restrained, editorial, industrial, or other chosen style family.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add style-fidelity checks to design-audit and the UI harness so each scenario can fail when it drifts back to generic product defaults.

gaps.symptom: The UI harness can now emit derived runtime traces, but Foundry's underlying design runtime still does not natively emit first-class provenance for style selection, exclusions, remediation steps, and dataset usage.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Benchmark routing can derive trace artifacts from scenario contracts, but the design engine itself still lacks a runtime-native provenance layer.
gaps.recommended_fix: Promote prompt-trace generation into the core design runtime and attach dataset ids, exclusions, remediation skills, and style reference ids automatically.

gaps.symptom: The UI harness can now derive remediation routing, but Foundry still lacks a native runtime that executes second-pass design remediation automatically after a weak first pass.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry has a command layer for design remediation and harness-level routing, but no shared runtime that can diagnose a surface and execute the right second-pass skills end-to-end.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add a first-class design remediation runtime that chains audit, layout repair, typography repair, intensity adjustment, simplification, and polish with explicit execution traces.

gaps.symptom: Foundry now has a first-class ui-testing route and a single benchmark runner, but the execution path still lives in repo-local harness scripts instead of a shared Foundry runtime or CLI executor.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Workflow routing and runner consolidation exist, but the benchmark runtime is still implemented in repo-local scripts rather than a reusable shared execution layer.
gaps.recommended_fix: Promote the repo-local benchmark runner into a native ui-testing runtime or CLI surface that the shared route can execute directly.

gaps.symptom: Responsive quality is visible in screenshots but not automatically scored by existing Foundry QA primitives.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Web QA captures evidence but lacks a built-in rubric for mobile re-composition quality.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add viewport-aware scoring hooks and responsive heuristics to the harness workflow.

gaps.symptom: Industrial control surfaces need better guardrails for warning-state density so risk colors do not flatten the hierarchy when several maintenance signals are active at once.
gaps.likely_root_cause: Foundry has not yet encoded a dedicated industrial warning strategy beyond generic enterprise severity treatments.
gaps.recommended_fix: Add industrial warning-state heuristics that separate watch, hold, and stop conditions through structure as well as color.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: The first atelier-stay layout let the hero headline dominate the spread so heavily that the supporting editorial modules looked underweighted until the type scale and column proportions were manually rebalanced.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry can produce technically valid editorial grids without checking whether headline mass and adjacent module density stay in visual parity.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add composition-balance checks to design-audit so oversized editorial headlines and underweighted companion columns fail review before screenshots are approved.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: The first coach-loop desktop shell reserved a full right-side grid track with no mounted content, creating a large dead zone until the shell structure was manually corrected.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry can validate CSS structure and visual style without checking whether major grid tracks are actually occupied by meaningful interface content.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add layout-occupancy checks to design-audit and the UI harness so empty reserved rails or underfilled desktop columns fail review.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: The first field-notes desktop shell reserved a page-level track that read like accidental left-spacing waste until the shell structure was collapsed into one real page canvas.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry can generate a nominally complex shell without checking whether page-level grid tracks are actually used by mounted content.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add page-shell occupancy checks so empty desktop tracks fail review before spacing debates start.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: Luxury concierge surfaces still need stronger heuristics for coupling narrative atmosphere to itinerary and host actions so they do not drift into static premium storytelling.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry’s current luxury-adjacent guidance is stronger on mood than on operational service design.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Expand service-led luxury patterns so host itineraries, rate ledgers, and request actions are first-class design moves.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: Neo-brutalist product surfaces can lose operability quickly if loud labels and offset stacks are not explicitly bounded around the transaction path.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry does not yet encode enough guardrails for high-intensity styles that must still preserve marketplace or commerce clarity.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add intensity-governance checks that verify loud styles still preserve the primary transaction path and do not bury critical actions.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: Industrial control surfaces need better guardrails for warning-state density so risk colors do not flatten the hierarchy when several maintenance signals are active at once.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry has not yet encoded a dedicated industrial warning strategy beyond generic enterprise severity treatments.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add industrial warning-state heuristics that separate watch, hold, and stop conditions through structure as well as color.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: The first pulse-festival desktop shell also reserved a dead page-level track, so the left-side hero felt like a spacing bug instead of intentional poster composition.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: The current audit loop does not distinguish between deliberate negative space and a shell grid that has no real peer content mounted into a reserved track.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Teach design-audit to fail poster-style shells when the page-level right track is empty instead of structurally counterweighted.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: Minimal SaaS surfaces remain vulnerable to collapsing into generic shadcn-like shells unless the preview lane and command ribbon are explicitly designed as product proof, not decorative support.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: Foundry has stronger anti-slop coverage for editorial or high-contrast surfaces than for deliberately restrained SaaS product language.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add stronger style-fidelity checks for restrained SaaS directions so generic startup fallback fails even when the UI is clean.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: The first remediated wealth-ops pass still produced an optical collision between the left control rail and the main hero canvas even though the CSS grid itself was valid.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: The harness and remediation loop do not yet score composition balance, rail-to-canvas tension, or headline collision risk as first-class review criteria.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add optical-collision and composition-balance checks to design-audit and the UI harness so dense layouts can fail before screenshots are approved.

scenarioSpecificNotes.symptom: The wealth-ops mobile view initially read like a compressed desktop stack instead of a staged mobile command surface with reprioritized sections and tighter action flow.
scenarioSpecificNotes.likely_root_cause: The fixture and harness do not yet enforce mobile-first re-composition rules for dense operational surfaces, so desktop zones simply collapse into one long feed.
scenarioSpecificNotes.recommended_fix: Add mobile re-staging checks to design-arrange and the UI harness so dense dashboards must reorder, compress, or defer sections instead of only stacking them.
